comparison: Both evaluate claims C5, C21, C64 about behavioral similarities between sleep induction methods. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with strong convergence of behavioral metrics. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the data but raising critical concerns about residual locomotor activity during optogenetic sleep that questions whether the methods truly produce similar behavioral effects.

Both evaluate claims C7, C33, C34, C36, C37 about THIP-induced downregulation of metabolism genes. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong RNA-seq and qRT-PCR validation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, accepting the transcriptomic analysis as appropriate but raising significant concerns that only ~9/19 genes show good correspondence between RNA-seq and qPCR, with variability issues in biological replicates.

Both evaluate claims C8, C38, C39, C40, C43 about optogenetic sleep upregulating genes including nicotinic receptors. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with RNA-seq and qRT-PCR validation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting appropriate analysis but highlighting that only 2/6 genes in Figure 7G show good RNA-seq/qPCR correspondence, with methodological reservations about the artificial manipulation.

Both evaluate claims C44-C50 about nAchRα knockout phenotypes. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive behavioral data showing consistent opposing phenotypes. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting these genetic validations as 'potentially interesting candidates for further studies' without specific critique.

Both evaluate claims C51, C52 about AkhR knockdown effects on sleep duration versus short sleep proportions. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, interpreting this as evidence for separate regulatory control. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting this functional validation as part of the candidate gene validation without specific challenge.

Both evaluate claims C53-C56 about circuit-specific nAchRα functions in R23E10 neurons. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with behavioral data showing consistency with whole-brain knockouts. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting these circuit-specific manipulations as additional validation without specific critique.

Both evaluate claims C22, C23 about sleep architecture and red light artifacts. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes concerns about potential confounds. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting these methodological observations as part of the behavioral characterization without challenge.

Both evaluate neural activity differences between methods (C6, C24, C25, C26, C82). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with converging calcium imaging evidence. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging clear illustration of neuronal activity differences and state-of-the-art techniques, though questioning potential errors in Figure 4C-D. OpenEval includes additional claims C29, C30, C66 not addressed in peer result R2.

Both address THIP-induced sleep characteristics. OpenEval R9 evaluates C27, C31, C32 about behavioral responsiveness and 'quiet' sleep state, finding SUPPORTED. Peer R3 evaluates overlapping claims C27, C29, C30, C31, C32 about detailed neural characterizations, also finding SUPPORTED. Both accept the brain imaging findings demonstrating THIP's distinct effects.

Both address lack of overlap in gene expression (C42 shared, C9-C10 in OpenEval only). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, emphasizing compelling evidence for fundamentally different molecular pathways. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging clear illustration of differences in gene expression, though noting this makes relationships with sleep state difficult to understand.

Partial overlap on claims about distinct transcriptomic effects. OpenEval R5 evaluates C9, C10, C42 about no gene overlap, finding SUPPORTED. Peer R7 evaluates C9, C10, C65, C66 about broader interpretation of active/quiet sleep forms, rating UNCERTAIN due to difficulty understanding relationships between transcriptomic/physiological changes and behavioral similarity, plus concerns about applicability to spontaneous sleep.

Both address control experiments. OpenEval R11 evaluates C35 (THIP+sleep prevention control), finding SUPPORTED. Peer R12 evaluates both C35 and C41 (time-course controls), finding SUPPORTED. Both accept these controls as appropriate, though peer reviewers note general validation concerns from their Concern 2.

Both evaluate C41 about short-duration optogenetic sleep having fewer transcriptomic effects. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting this temporal control distinguishes sleep-related changes from immediate effects. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting this as part of appropriate transcriptomic analysis without specific challenge.

Minimal overlap (C65 only). OpenEval R13 evaluates C65, C73, C74 about THIP rapidly inducing quiet sleep, finding SUPPORTED based on brain imaging. Peer R7 includes C65 in broader evaluation of active/quiet sleep interpretation (C9, C10, C65, C66), rating UNCERTAIN due to conceptual concerns about relating transcriptomic/physiological differences to behavioral similarity.
